Ok, now all this in consideration, if the one single purpose to be stated for the eventbus architecture is to: 'express all actions as if the entire application were immediately a multiplayer game' can you see the massive red flags this impedes on. Think about the operation crtical and fundamentals of what that means: the application should behave in a way where even thought it ISNT multiplayer today, when in future times come, its not a foreign body; 

ok now this opens a fucking whiplash to the current state if you see it as i see it, and im sure its clear as day. Why isnt every 'event' that can happen, and does happen, not pass here. 

what is an 'event' in my eyes

well, an event is anything at all that changes. An event is not a undo or redo history. it is a ledger of what happened. When it happened. Why it happened, and by whom it happened from. This gives events a two tone architecture in my pov;

you have

events that are actions 
events that are reports

action based events: the user painted this, the user removed that, the user dragged this, the user did that. These are all, your traditional 'undo/redo' event history. These are the things that a ctrl z and y are to exist for.

report based events: this is everything. This covers action based events also, why, because this is the audit trail. this reports things like 'changed color to red' ' selected a new brush' 'painted a stroke' -> 'undid paint stroke' -> 'redid paint stroke' -> ....

so where that report based events can become circular, i could forever do one stroke, and sit and undo and redo it all day long, my action based events have their one clear undo and redo state, but everytime i do it, collectively it says i did it, and that doesnt go anywhere. 


why does this matter at all if there is no multiplayer right now: well there wil lbe in the future, but also as it stands basically we have what should be one coherent system and its just stepping out of line. 

to me, i see the application and the user like a house. The house has glass walls, i can see inside of it just fine, but for me to change anything in there at all, i have to somehow get inside, and there is only 1 door
resolution: Analyzed the user's eventbus doctrine against the active editor and the ruled multiplayer/event-sourced direction. Confirmed the central contradiction: the documented bus contract says all mutations enter through dispatch, while current React and Zig systems mutate first through multiple private paths and only sometimes append after-the-fact receipts. Formalized the two-tone model (reversible action ledger plus immutable report ledger), the single-door invariants, undo/redo causality semantics, multiplayer implications, gesture granularity, and why coverage-only dispatch patches would worsen rather than solve the architecture. Read-only analysis; no source changes.
